column1: # duration acceptance vectors, from the RFC 3339 Appendix A ABNF.
# Components appear in canonical order with no gaps, and weeks stand alone. The
# official suite's optional/format/duration.json carries 36 string cases and
# already pins the contiguous-chain rejections P1Y2D and PT1H2S, which the rows
# below restate so the chain rules read whole in one place. What it leaves open
# is the week alternative's exclusivity beyond P1Y2W, and a partial date part
# before a time: every valid date-then-time case it carries runs the chain down
# to the day, so P1YT1H below is the first with a year and no day.
# FuzzFormatDurationVsABNF carries the depth beyond all of it.
# Row format: see loadVectorFile in vectors_test.go.

column3: dur-year with its optional dur-month absent
dur-time with no dur-date before it
a zero quantity is well formed
dur-year = 1*DIGIT "Y" [dur-month], so year to day skips a link
dur-week is an alternative to dur-date, not a prefix of it

column1: # The week alternative's exclusivity, the composition of a date with a time,
# and the two productions that spell a month and a minute with the same

column3: duration = "P" (dur-date / dur-time / dur-week), so dur-week admits no time
weeks do not combine with days in either order
M outside dur-time is dur-month, so this counts months
the same letter inside dur-time is dur-minute, so this counts minutes
dur-hour = 1*DIGIT "H" [dur-minute], so hour to second skips a link
1*DIGIT is ASCII; these are Arabic-Indic digits
